reset$

The reset$ stream emits a notification whenever a FeatureCell is reset. This stream provides a lifecycle signal that indicates the FeatureCell’s state has been cleared and returned to a neutral baseline while remaining fully initialized and operable.

Stream Contract Summary

  • Emits each time the FeatureCell is reset
  • Does not terminate the FeatureCell lifecycle
  • Does not complete on emission
  • May emit multiple times over the FeatureCell’s lifetime
  • Does not emit state values or snapshots

The reset$ stream defines a non-terminal lifecycle signal. It does not participate in pipeline execution, does not influence control flow, and does not suppress future updates. Its sole responsibility is to notify observers that a reset operation has occurred.

Note

Unlike destroyed$, the reset$ stream does not indicate teardown. After a reset event, the FeatureCell remains active and may continue processing updates, executing pipelines, and emitting state snapshots.

Property Contract
Property Definition
Member Description
reset$

type:

  • Observable<void>

emissions:

  • Emits on each reset
 Emits whenever the FeatureCell is reset. Signals that state and error information have been cleared while preserving the FeatureCell’s initialized runtime surface.
Example

The reset$ observable allows consumers to react to FeatureCell resets. This is commonly used to clear derived UI state, reset local caches, or reinitialize external resources that depend on FeatureCell state.

Example: Observing FeatureCell Reset

{{`this.vault.reset$
  .subscribe(() => {
    console.info('FeatureCell was reset');
  });`}}
 
{{`employeeCell.reset$
  .subscribe(() => {
    console.info('FeatureCell was reset');
  });`}}

What this does

  • Subscribes to the FeatureCell reset signal
  • Receives a notification each time reset() is called
  • Continues listening across multiple resets
  • Does not receive state values or snapshots

This stream is ideal for coordinating cleanup or reinitialization logic that must run whenever FeatureCell state is cleared, without requiring FeatureCell teardown.
